sentence: The thymus is a small lymphoid organ in the upper chest, lying behind the breastbone in the mediastinum.
note: MedlinePlus: small organ in the upper chest under the breastbone. StatPearls: superior retrosternal mediastinum. OpenStax: primary lymphoid organ.

sentence: It has two lobes and, before birth and in childhood, helps the body make T lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell that helps protect against infection.
note: StatPearls: two lobes. MedlinePlus: before birth and in childhood the thymus helps make white blood cells that protect against infection. OpenStax: T cells mature.

sentence: At puberty the thymus begins to shrink and is gradually replaced by fat, so it is usually small by adulthood.
note: MedlinePlus: at puberty the thymus starts getting smaller and is replaced by fat; usually small in adults. StatPearls: fat replacement after puberty.

sentence: Superior and anterior mediastinum, behind the breastbone
note: StatPearls: bilobed structure in the superior and anterior mediastinum; superior retrosternal mediastinum. MedlinePlus: under the breastbone.

sentence: Two lobes that converge near the level of the manubrium; number, size and position vary
note: StatPearls: the two lobes converge near the sternal manubrium; variation in lobe number, size and position is common.

sentence: Each lobe is divided into lobules with an outer cortex and an inner medulla
note: Returned search summary and standard textbook histology; no single retrievable human-thymus URL was returned for this wording.

sentence: Inferior thyroid artery and branches of the internal thoracic arteries
note: StatPearls thymectomy: inferior thyroid artery and internal thoracic branches are the main sources; smaller pericardiophrenic and intercostal branches.

sentence: Veins follow the arteries; a large posterior vein enters the left innominate vein
note: StatPearls thymectomy: venous drainage follows the arteries; a large posterior vein drains into the left innominate vein.

sentence: Maturation and selection of T lymphocytes
note: OpenStax: the thymus is a primary lymphoid organ where T lymphocytes proliferate and mature; cells reacting to self-antigen are removed.

sentence: Shrinks from puberty and is replaced by fat
note: MedlinePlus: at puberty the thymus gets smaller and is replaced by fat. StatPearls: involution after puberty.

sentence: The thymus lies in the superior part of the mediastinum, behind the sternum.
note: StatPearls: located in the superior portion of the retrosternal mediastinum; a bilobed structure in the superior and anterior mediastinum.

sentence: The mediastinum is the part of the chest that lies between the sternum and the spinal column and between the lungs.
note: MedlinePlus: the mediastinum is the part of the chest between the sternum and the spinal column, and between the lungs.

sentence: The thymus is a bilobed organ, and its two lobes converge near the level of the manubrium of the sternum.
note: StatPearls: the two lobes converge near the level of the sternal manubrium; thymectomy chapter calls it bilobed.

sentence: Extensions of the thymus can rise into the neck towards the thyroid, and the number, size and position of the lobes vary a good deal between people.
note: StatPearls: cervical extensions can rise toward the thyroid; anatomic variation in lobe number, size and position is common.

sentence: The two lobes form separately early in gestation and then migrate to fuse.
note: StatPearls: the lobes form separately early in gestation and migrate to fuse.

sentence: Each lobe is divided into lobules, and each lobule has an outer cortex and an inner medulla.
note: Returned search summary and standard textbook histology; no single retrievable human-thymus URL was returned for this wording.

sentence: Immature T cells, called thymocytes, leave the bone marrow and mature largely in the thymus.
note: OpenStax: the immature T cell, called a thymocyte, leaves the bone marrow and matures largely in the thymus gland.

sentence: The medulla is made up mainly of medullary thymic epithelial cells and dendritic cells.
note: Returned summary: the thymic medulla is mainly composed of medullary thymic epithelial cells and dendritic cells.

sentence: It contains concentric, whorled structures called Hassall's corpuscles, which are formed from epithelial cells.
note: Returned summary: Hassall's corpuscles are concentric whorled structures found only in the thymic medulla, formed from medullary epithelial cells.

sentence: The arterial supply of the thymus is variable.
note: StatPearls thymectomy: arterial supply is variable.

sentence: The main sources are the inferior thyroid artery and branches of the internal thoracic arteries, with smaller contributions from the pericardiophrenic and intercostal arteries.
note: StatPearls thymectomy: inferior thyroid artery and internal thoracic branches; smaller contributions from pericardiophrenic and intercostal arteries.

sentence: Venous drainage follows the arteries, and a large posterior vein drains into the left innominate (brachiocephalic) vein.
note: StatPearls thymectomy: venous drainage follows the arteries; a large posterior vein drains into the left innominate vein. Brachiocephalic is the modern synonym.

sentence: The blood supply, lymphatic drainage and innervation of each lobe remain separate throughout life, even after the lobes have fused.
note: StatPearls: blood supply, lymphatic drainage and innervation stay separate throughout life, even after fusion.

sentence: The thymus is a primary lymphoid organ in which T lymphocytes proliferate and mature.
note: OpenStax: the thymus is a primary lymphoid organ where T lymphocytes proliferate and mature.

sentence: Thymocytes are screened for tolerance there: cells that react with the body's own antigens are removed by negative selection, and only a small minority of thymocytes leave the thymus as mature, functional T cells.
note: OpenStax: thymocytes are screened for tolerance; cells reacting with self-antigen are removed by negative selection; only a small fraction leave as functional T cells.

sentence: The autoimmune regulator (AIRE) protein, which works mainly in the thymus, helps eliminate T cells that could otherwise attack the body's own tissues.
note: MedlinePlus Genetics: in the thymus the AIRE protein destroys T cells that would otherwise cause autoimmune damage.

sentence: The mature T cells include helper, regulatory and cytotoxic types, which go on to take part in adaptive immune responses elsewhere, for example in lymph nodes.
note: OpenStax: major T cell types are helper, regulatory and cytotoxic; lymph nodes are sites where T cells mount adaptive responses.

sentence: The thymus is active and growing in childhood, when it makes white blood cells that fight infection.
note: MedlinePlus: the thymus is active and growing in childhood and makes white blood cells to fight infections.

sentence: At puberty it starts to get smaller and is replaced by fat, and it is usually small by adulthood.
note: MedlinePlus: at puberty the thymus starts getting smaller and is replaced by fat; it is usually small by adulthood.

sentence: This shrinkage, called involution, is thought to result from rising androgen levels in the circulation during puberty.
note: StatPearls: involution is thought to result from rising circulating androgen levels during puberty, with replacement of thymic tissue by fat.

sentence: On CT scans of adults, the appearance of the thymus changes with age as it is replaced by fat.
note: Returned summary of CT studies: thymic attenuation declines with age, reflecting fatty replacement. Title: Normal Thymus in Adults, Appearance on CT and Associations with Age.

sentence: In people with myasthenia gravis, described below, a chest CT scan is commonly used to check the thymus.
note: NHS trust leaflets: a chest CT scan is commonly used to check the thymus in myasthenia gravis.

sentence: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune condition in which antibodies interfere with the signal from nerves to muscles, causing weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest.
note: NHS trust leaflets: autoimmune condition; antibodies interfere with the signal from nerves to muscles; weakness worse with activity, better with rest.

sentence: Eye symptoms such as drooping eyelids and double vision are often the first to appear, and other muscles can be affected, causing problems with swallowing, speech or breathing.
note: NHS trust leaflets: drooping eyelids and double vision often appear first; swallowing, speech and breathing difficulties when other muscles are involved.

sentence: Symptoms can be made worse by fatigue, overuse of a muscle, hot weather, infections or stress.
note: NHS trust leaflets: symptoms can worsen with fatigue, overuse of a muscle, hot weather, infections or stress.

sentence: Surgery to remove the thymus (thymectomy) can reduce the symptoms of myasthenia gravis, possibly by rebalancing the immune system.
note: MedlinePlus: thymectomy, surgery to remove the thymus gland, can reduce the symptoms of myasthenia gravis, possibly by rebalancing the immune system.

sentence: Cancer of the thymus, including thymoma and thymic carcinoma, is rare.
note: MedlinePlus: cancer of the thymus is rare. NCI: thymoma and thymic carcinoma treatment summary.

sentence: Surgery to remove the tumour is the most common treatment, and radiation therapy, chemotherapy, chemoradiation and hormone therapy are other options.
note: MedlinePlus: most common treatment is surgery. NCI: options include surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, chemoradiation and hormone therapy.

sentence: Treatment of an early-stage (stage I) thymoma is surgery.
note: NCI: treatment of stage I thymoma is surgery.

sentence: Some people are born with an underdeveloped thymus.
note: Clinical guideline title and text address 22q11.2 deletion syndrome and other defects in thymic development.

sentence: In 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, also called DiGeorge syndrome, the thymus can be underdeveloped (hypoplastic), which can lower the number of T cells in the blood.
note: Returned text: 22q11.2 deletion (DiGeorge) causes thymic hypoplasia that can lead to low peripheral T cell numbers.

sentence: The effect on immunity depends mainly on whether the thymus is hypoplastic, severely hypoplastic or absent (aplastic).
note: Returned text: clinical impact on the immune system depends primarily on whether the thymus is hypoplastic, severely hypoplastic or aplastic.
